basic_identification.full_title: Machining Allowances and Tolerances for Open Die Steel Forgings (Part 1: Carbon and Low Alloy Steel Forgings; Part 2: High Alloy Steel Forgings)
basic_identification.sector_category: Metallurgical Engineering / Alloy Steels and Forgings (finalized by the Alloy Steels and Forgings Sectional Committee under the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Alloy Steels and Forgings Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies the machining allowances (minimum over-metal thicknesses) and dimensional tolerances for open die steel forgings. Part 1 covers forgings manufactured from carbon and low alloy steels, while Part 2 covers forgings manufactured from high alloy steels. These values are designed to ensure that forgings contain sufficient excess metal to clean up completely during subsequent machining without leaving scale, decarburisation, or surface flaws on the finished component.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Dimensional and Quality Reference Standard. Unlike structural steel products or builders hardware which are subject to mandatory statutory Quality Control Orders (QCOs), IS 10604 is a reference specification for machining and dimensions. However, manufacturing compliance to its stated allowances and tolerances is universally required across Indian public and private sector heavy engineering, railways, defense, and shipyard procurement tenders to ensure proper material cleanup and dimensional alignment after machining. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.

requirements.detail: Forgings are divided into two distinct parts based on alloy concentration: Part 1 regulates carbon and low alloy steel forgings (alloy content typically <= 5% total), and Part 2 regulates high alloy steel forgings (alloy content > 5% total) which have different thermal contraction behavior.

The machining allowance is defined as the minimal thickness of extra metal (over-metal) left on the raw forging's outer envelope. This thickness must be sufficient to ensure that during subsequent material removal, all hot-rolling scale, decarburized surface layers, and surface micro-cracks are completely removed, leaving a pristine finished surface.

Enforces strict limits on the maximum allowable dimensional deviations (positive and negative tolerances) on nominal forged dimensions (including diameter, thickness, length, and width) to accommodate tool wear and uneven shrinkage.

The forgings must be sound and free from piping, cracks, laminations, seams, deep laps, and slag inclusions. Visual and non-destructive testing (such as magnetic particle flaw detection per IS 3703) must verify surface soundness.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 10604 : 1983 (Reaffirmed 2023) is the national Indian Standard specification establishing machining allowances and dimensional tolerances for open die (free) steel forgings. It is divided into Part 1 for carbon and low alloy steel forgings and Part 2 for high alloy steel forgings. These guidelines define the minimum excess metal ('over-metal') that must remain on the raw forged envelope so that all hot-scale, decarburized skin, and surface cracks are completely cleared during final machining. Crucially, to account for bending and warping during hot deformation, the standard enforces a sliding penalty scale that increases both allowances and tolerances by up to 75% for long, slender forgings where the ratio of length to section diameter exceeds 7.
